headline: Twelve months after the sandeel closure, the seabird numbers are the first thing to move
standfirst: Kittiwake productivity on two monitored colonies is up sharply. Whether the closure caused it is a harder question.

image.alt: Kittiwakes nesting on a sea cliff

body.text: Productivity at the two long-monitored colonies rose to 0.81 and 0.74 chicks per pair, against a five-year mean nearer 0.5. Both sit within foraging range of ground closed to sandeel fishing last spring.

The caveat is that it was also a good year for sea temperature at exactly the wrong depth for sandeel predators, which muddies the attribution considerably. A second good year would settle a lot of arguments.
